lessons.title: XGBoost with Optuna tuning
lessons.tried: A gradient-boosted model on the TF-IDF features plus five engineered text features (length, redaction count, dollar amounts, weekday), tuned with 13 Optuna trials, then trained on all the data on a Colab GPU.
lessons.result: Validation weighted F1 0.590 against 0.605 for the TF-IDF + logistic regression baseline (macro-F1 0.454 against 0.472), in 33 minutes against 16. None of its 15 most important features was an engineered one.
lessons.learned: On sparse text a linear model is hard to beat, and the features I added carried nothing beyond the words. That pointed to a model that reads context, which is where the LoRA fine-tune came from. I also did not save XGBoost's vectorizer, so the model could not be reused; every run since saves what it needs to be reproduced.

lessons.title: Merging confusable labels (26 to 19 classes)
lessons.tried: Merged 12 confusable labels into 5 groups and retrained the baseline on the merged labels.
lessons.result: Macro-F1 0.4777 for the retrained model against 0.4801 for the original model simply scored on the merged labels: training on them added nothing. The merged task is dominated by one large class, so its weighted F1 looks high without the model getting better.
lessons.learned: Merging changes the task, not the model, and the weak classes were a long tail of small ones, not the ones I merged. Later I merged just three overlapping credit-reporting issues for the served taxonomy as a labelled product decision, and the page shows both class counts side by side.

lessons.title: An LLM choosing the label for unsure complaints
lessons.tried: For complaints the classifier was unsure about, an LLM (openai/gpt-oss-120b) chose among at most five candidate labels, shown the similar past complaints.
lessons.result: On 150 random validation complaints (24 classes) the LLM was right 39% of the time when it answered, against 43% for the classifier's own guess on the same complaints; on the 26 classes 47% against 55%. It called itself high-confidence on 99% of its answers.
lessons.learned: The right label was among the candidates 85% of the time, so the limit was not a missing option: the labels overlap and the LLM does not know how people label them. Its job is now a note for the human reviewer, and it can never set a label.

lessons.title: Blending models
lessons.tried: Averaging the probabilities of XGBoost and the logistic regression, then of LoRA and the logistic regression.
lessons.result: The XGBoost blend could not be built: its vectorizer was not saved, and rebuilding it on my laptop gave a different vocabulary, so the saved model read the wrong columns (its score fell from 0.45 to 0.21 in a check that stopped the run). The LoRA plus logistic regression blend gained only +0.0046 macro-F1 on validation.
lessons.learned: A gain that small does not justify serving two models. Reproducibility is part of the model: a saved model without the exact preprocessing that produced its inputs cannot be used.

final.classifier_label: Credit reporting | Dispute, accuracy or use of report
final.summary: The user reports a generic problem with their account and lack of response, which could relate to a checking/savings account issue, a credit‑reporting dispute, or simply an 'Other' miscellaneous problem. The ambiguity arises because the complaint lacks specifics about the account type, the nature of the problem, or any mention of credit reporting or fraud. Clarifying whether the issue involves unauthorized activity, a credit report dispute, or a standard banking service request would resolve the label choice.
